class.name: SpineSprite2D
class.brief_description: A node for animating and rendering a Spine skeleton to a 2D scene.
class.description: A Spine sprite node is the main node type used to animate and render a Spine skeleton in a 2D scene. The Spine sprite gets its skeleton, texture atlas data, and animation mixes from a [code]SpineSkeletonDataResource[/code]. The skeleton data resource can and should be shared across multiple Spine sprites to save resources. The Spine sprite provides a [code]SpineAnimationState[/code] via [code]get_animation_state()[/code] through which it can be animated. The Spine sprite also provides acccess to the underlying [code]SpineSkeleton[/code] via [code]get_skeleton[/code] which allows querying bones, slots, constraints, and other parts of the skeleton. The [code]SpineSkeleton[/code] from [code]get_skeleton()[/code] controls the active skin. The [code]SpineAnimationState[/code] from [code]get_animation_state()[/code] controls playback. To play an animation from code, call [code]get_animation_state().set_animation("walk", true, 0)[/code]. The second argument sets looping. The third argument is the track index. Track 0 is the main layer. Call [code]get_animation_state().add_animation("jump", 0, false, 0)[/code] to queue an animation after the current one on the same track. To switch skin from code, call [code]get_skeleton().set_skin_by_name("full-skins/girl")[/code] with a skin name from your skeleton data. Pass [code]null[/code] to [code]get_skeleton().set_skin()[/code] for the default skin. For mix-and-match, create a skin with [code]new_skin("custom-skin")[/code], add parts with [code]SpineSkin.add_skin(get_skeleton().get_data().find_skin("hair/brown"))[/code], then call [code]get_skeleton().set_skin(custom_skin)[/code]. After a skin switch, call [code]get_skeleton().set_slots_to_setup_pose()[/code] so slot attachments refresh. When [code]update_mode[/code] is [code]Manual[/code], call [code]update_skeleton(delta)[/code] each frame after you change skin or animation. To insert other nodes into the drawing order of the Spine sprite's slots, a [code]SpineSlotNode2D[/code] can be used. This allows attaching particle systems, collision shapes, and other Godot nodes to specific slots and bones of the Spine sprite's skeleton. The Spine sprite allows overriding the internal materials through 4 material properties. If set, these materials will be used instead of the default internal materials for all attachments. For more fine grained control, a [code]SpineSlotNode2D[/code] can override the material of the attachment on a specific slot. By default, a Spine sprite is updated during the standard [code]process[/code] update. It can be set to update during the physics update via the [code]process_mode[/code] property. It can also be set to be updated manually, in which case [code]update_skeleton[/code] must be called so the internal animation state is updated and applied to the skeleon. The Spine sprite provides the method to query ([code]get_global_bone_transform()[/code]) and set ([code]set_global_bone_transform[/code]) a bone's global transform. This can be used to have another node follow a bone, or have a bone follow e.g. the mouse or another node. Alternatively, a [code]SpineBoneNode2D[/code] can be used to achieve the same, without having to manually update and synchronize transforms. The Spine sprite provides signals to listen for animation state events, such as an animation having completed or when a user defined event occurred. It also provides signals before the animations state is updated and applied, and before and after the world transforms of bones have been computed, allowing to modify the underlying skeleton before these actions happen. In editor mode, the Spine sprite provides properties to show debugging information, such as bone and slot names on hover, regions and meshes, and so forth. This can be used to inspect a skeleton and its hierarchy in the editor viewport. To animate a Spine sprite via the Godot animation player, add [code]SpineAnimationTrack[/code] keys to an [code]AnimationPlayer[/code].

method.name: get_animation_state
method.description: Returns the animation state for this sprite. Use [code]set_animation()[/code] and [code]add_animation()[/code] on the result to change playback from code.

method.name: get_skeleton
method.description: Returns the live skeleton for this sprite. Use [code]set_skin()[/code], [code]set_skin_by_name()[/code], and [code]set_slots_to_setup_pose()[/code] on the result to change skin from code.

method.name: get_time_scale
method.description: Returns the animation playback speed multiplier applied during [code]update_skeleton()[/code].

method.name: new_skin
method.description: Creates a new empty skin on the skeleton. Add attachments from other skins with [code]SpineSkin.add_skin()[/code], then pass the result to [code]get_skeleton().set_skin()[/code].

method.name: on_skeleton_data_changed
method.description: Reloads internal skeleton and animation objects after [code]skeleton_data_res[/code] changes. Called automatically when the resource updates.

method.name: rebuild_spine_objects
method.description: Rebuilds the skeleton, animation state, and mesh children from [code]skeleton_data_res[/code].

method.name: schedule_skeleton_rebuild
method.description: Queues a skeleton rebuild for the next frame. The sprite calls this when skeleton data or atlas resources change.

method.name: set_global_bone_transform
method.description: Sets a bone's global transform. This must be done before the skeleton world transforms are computed.

method.name: set_time_scale
method.description: Sets the animation playback speed multiplier applied during [code]update_skeleton()[/code].

method.name: teardown_mesh_children
method.description: Removes all [code]SpineMesh2D[/code] child nodes. The sprite calls this during teardown or resource reload.

method.name: teardown_spine_objects
method.description: Destroys internal skeleton and animation state objects. The sprite calls this during resource reload or shutdown.

method.name: update_skeleton
method.description: Updates and applies the animation state, then updates the world transforms. Only needed for the manual processing mode.

signal.name: _internal_spine_objects_invalidated
signal.description: Emitted when internal Spine skeleton or animation objects are destroyed and recreated. Advanced tooling uses this to drop stale references.

signal.name: animation_completed
signal.description: Invoked every time this entry's animation completes a loop. This may occur during mixing (after interrupt). If this entry's [code]get_mixing_to()[/code] is not null, this entry is mixing out (it is not the current entry). Because this event is triggered at the end of [code]AnimationState.apply[/code], any animations set in response to the event won't be applied until the next time the AnimationState is applied.

signal.name: animation_disposed
signal.description: Invoked when this entry will be disposed. This may occur without the entry ever being set as the current entry. References to the entry should not be kept after [code]dispose[/code] is called, as it may be destroyed or reused.

signal.name: animation_ended
signal.description: Invoked when this entry will never be applied again. This only occurs if this entry has previously been set as the current entry (start was invoked).

signal.name: animation_event
signal.description: Invoked when this entry's animation triggers an event. This may occur during mixing (after interrupt), see [code]TrackEntry.get_event_threshold()[/code]. Because this event is triggered at the end of {@link AnimationState#apply(Skeleton)}, any animations set in response to the event won't be applied until the next time the AnimationState is applied.

signal.name: animation_interrupted
signal.description: Invoked when another entry has replaced this entry as the current entry. This entry may continue being applied for mixing.

signal.name: animation_started
signal.description: Invoked when this entry has been set as the current entry. {@link #end(TrackEntry)} will occur when this entry will no longer be applied.

signal.name: before_animation_state_apply
signal.description: Invoked before the animation state is applied to the skeleton.

signal.name: before_animation_state_update
signal.description: Invoked before the animation state is updated.

signal.name: before_world_transforms_change
signal.description: Invoked before the world transforms are computed.

signal.name: world_transforms_changed
signal.description: Invoked after the world transforms have been computed.
